<thought>Based on the observed isotopic envelope: a relatively strong M+1 peak (~16 % of the base) indicates the presence of many carbon atoms (C‑13 natural abundance ≈1.1 % per carbon). A modest M+2 peak (~4–5 % of the base) matches the natural abundance of 34S (≈4.2 %). No ~33 % M+2 (Cl) or ~100 % M+2 (Br) patterns are seen, so chlorine and bromine are not definitively present. Thus the elements that can be definitively identified from the isotope distribution are carbon and sulfur.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'S']</final_answer>
